findings.label: Calf muscle hypertrophy
findings.evidence: Hypertrophy of calf muscles (case 2) Figure showing the prominent calf muscle hypertrophy

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the posterior lower legs of a patient from a case series on autosomal recessive Becker's form of myotonia congenita; caption explicitly states prominent calf muscle hypertrophy (case 2), and the in-text mentions hypertrophy of upper and lower limbs with Herculean appearance. Muscle hypertrophy (including prominent calves) is a classic manifestation of myotonia congenita. Skin is visible and adequately lit, judged medium; no ethnicity stated in caption or in-text; patients described as children. [raw subtype: autosomal_recessive_becker]

in_text_mentions: Both children had easy fatigability for outdoor games and initially approached several hospitals. Vitamin D3 and calcium supplementation was evident as per history, which did not alleviate the symptoms over the period. However, in both cases, the symptoms did not coincide with loss of sensation. In addition, there are no neurocutaneous markers. Following examination, the girl's vitals were found to be stable. Hypertrophy was noticed in their upper and lower limbs (shoulder and calf muscles) (Figures 2, 3), with Herculean appearance and negative Grower's sign.
